experiment: PREDICT-THEN-VERIFY PROVISIONING, DISCRIMINATIVE TEST (Qwen2.5-7B on Anvil). The Sonnet run (e12, prereg b4e6b2f) was judged FAIL per its letter but was NON-DISCRIMINATIVE: Sonnet's surface is floor-degenerate (tau 0.11-0.34, decay complete by k=1), so the naive nearest-cell predictor ties ANY predictor -- and that degeneracy is itself a finding (budget cannot buy retention on frontier). The fair, discriminative home of the provisioning law is where the budget law BINDS: Qwen-7B, whose prior budget sweep (n=100, in-repo) shows tau = 0.54/1.00/1.48/2.39 at B=8/16/25/50 -- a live gradient where a naive predictor must fail at mid-decay held-out cells and the law can genuinely win or lose.
design: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (hf, 4-bit-free full precision on A100), temp=0, neutral handoff, 32 probes/cell (8/type, ndist=7 mixed; NOTE regime matches e8/e12 mixed-distractor style, NOT the old budget-sweep same-type regime, so tau values may shift -- the law fits its own calibration; priors only guided grid design). CALIBRATION: B in {8,16,40} x k in {0,1,2,4}. HELD-OUT (fixed in advance): (25,2),(25,4) budget interpolation; (64,1),(64,4),(64,8) budget extrapolation 1.6x beyond grid; (16,8) depth extrapolation 2x. Naive baseline = nearest calibration cell (same rule as e12). PROVISIONING INVERSION: target T=0.5 at k_t=2 -- chosen A PRIORI so the expected B* lands in [20,60] per the prior sweep, INSIDE the law's validity range (B below content length ~60 words); beyond that the budget stops binding (the Sonnet saturation finding), and no engineer provisions outside spec range.
metric: MAE of law predictions on 6 held-out cells vs naive-baseline MAE; provisioning |S_obs(B*,2) - 0.5|.

PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.LAW_PREDICTS: mae_law <= 0.10 AND mae_law < mae_naive AND provisioning |err| <= 0.15. -> Method B validated where the budget law binds: the half-life surface is an a-priori provisioning rule (measure a few cells -> predict/configure any pipeline). Paper method = provisioning law scoped to the budget-bound regime, with Sonnet saturation as the honest frontier boundary.
PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.PARTIAL: mae_law <= 0.18 AND (mae_law < mae_naive OR provisioning |err| <= 0.15). -> law predictive but coarse; scope claims per-cell honestly (e.g. interpolation-only if extrapolation cells miss).
PRE_REGISTERED_READOUT.FAIL: mae_law > 0.18 OR mae_naive <= mae_law. -> even in its natural regime the surface does not predict; Method B falls entirely; paper is characterization-only. No further regimes will be tried (this is the designated discriminative test).

predictions.point: Expect S0 ~ 0.95-1.0, aggregate floor f ~ 0.15-0.3, beta ~ 0.6-1.0 (prior 0.82), tau(16) ~ 0.8-1.5. Mid-decay held-out cells ((25,2),(64,1),(64,4)) are where law should beat naive decisively (naive must copy a wrong-budget neighbor). (16,8) likely near floor (less discriminative). B* expected ~25-55.
predictions.risk: (1) Regime shift (mixed distractors) may move tau off the priors -- the law self-calibrates but B* could land outside [20,60]; if B* > 64 the inversion enters the saturation zone and may miss high like Sonnet -- report as-is. (2) n=32/cell binomial SE ~0.09. (3) Anvil job/env risks (CRLF, offline HF cache, fairshare queue).
predictions.honest_limits: single model regime for the discriminative claim; aggregate-over-types surface; one inversion target. If LAW_PREDICTS, the claim is 'provisioning law validated on a budget-bound model, saturation-bounded on frontier' -- NOT 'works everywhere'.
